description.p: Keystone is an on-screen keyboard for desktop Linux. It floats above your other windows and types into whichever application has focus, so it works with touchscreens, pen input, or a mouse when a physical keyboard is not available or not practical.

It is built for everyday use rather than kiosk duty: the window remembers its size and position, it can shrink to a compact layout or expand to a full keyboard with a numeric keypad, and it stays out of the way in the system tray until you need it.

ul.li: Compact and full keyboard layouts, switchable at runtime
Word completion with a built-in dictionary
Accented and special characters via long-press
Themes, including several dark variants, with support for custom theme packs
Tray icon with show, hide, and toggle controls
Command-line control of a running instance for scripting and shortcuts

description.p: Keystone runs on GNOME and KDE Plasma, under both X11 and Wayland.

description.p: First public beta. Keystone is feature-complete for everyday typing but is still under active development, and settings or defaults may change before the 1.0 release.
